- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
- Adds tokenizer config child class for multimodal specific fields
- `build_tokenizer()` should accept with an appropriate `TokenizerConfig` instance
- Avoid re-running `build_tokenizer()` if it was already set as a global
- When routing through `initialize_megatron()` -> `initialize_runtime_services()` , tokenizer is created via TokenizerConfig and padded vocab size is updated on the config rather than global args


:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

Static review of all 20 changed files found six issues below and two additional inline findings. Tests and suggested corrections were not executed; please verify the proposed changes before adopting them.

### [P1] Defer the new imports until runtime tokenizer construction

**Failure:** A fresh `import megatron.training` now enters the model/configuration dependency graph before the package has initialized its public exports. The new [module-level imports](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/global_vars.py#L11-L13) create the cycle `global_vars → models → hybrid → vocab_utils → config → container → models`: [Hybrid imports vocabulary utilities before defining its config](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/models/hybrid.py#L26-L34), while [container imports the not-yet-exported model configs](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/config/container.py#L37). This causes an import-time failure across training and inference entrypoints, before initialization can run.

**Correction:** Remove all three new module-level imports and put them inside [_build_tokenizer](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/global_vars.py#L306-L318), after its docstring:

```python
from megatron.training.models.gpt import GPTModelConfig
from megatron.training.models.hybrid import HybridModelConfig
from megatron.training.vocab_utils import build_tokenizer_and_pad_vocab_size
```

This preserves the existing lazy-bootstrap boundary while retaining both typed-model dispatch and legacy-provider fallback.

**Proposed checks:** In fresh interpreters with the supported dependencies installed, import `megatron.training`, `megatron.training.config`, and both model config classes successfully. Then exercise `_build_tokenizer` with GPT, Hybrid, and `model=None`; retain config-owned divisibility/TP settings for typed models and args-derived settings for legacy providers.

### [P1] Preserve multimodal tokenizer choices in the CLI

**Failure:** Removing both multimodal values from [TokenizerConfig.tokenizer_type](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/config/training_config.py#L739-L750) also removes them from argparse: [_add_tokenizer_args still generates its choices from TokenizerConfig](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f6332eb9e45e7bbb31625919ca703677ce128ec2/megatron/training/arguments.py#L3240-L3244), not the new subclass. After the duplicate-option problem noted inline is fixed, `--tokenizer-type MultimodalTokenizer` and `--tokenizer-type NullMultimodalTokenizer` are rejected as invalid choices before `tokenizer_config_from_args` can select the subclass.

**Correction:** Restore these two choices in the base declaration used to generate the CLI; the subclass can still own the multimodal-specific fields. The relevant portion should remain:

```python
"TikTokenizer",
"MultimodalTokenizer",
"NullTokenizer",
"NullMultimodalTokenizer",
```
